The match, scheduled for the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid at 8.45pm Nigerian time, offers England an opportunity to avenge their recent defeat to Spain and secure the group’s top position.
Both nations have already qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals, but the battle for first place remains unresolved, with Spain holding a three-point advantage.
Spain lead Group A3 with 15 points from five matches, having won all their fixtures, while Thomas Tuchel’s England occupy second place with 12 points from four victories and one defeat.
The equation is straightforward for both sides. Spain need only a draw to retain top spot, while England must win to finish above the European champions, subject to the competition’s tie-break rules.
For England, the encounter is also an opportunity to respond to their 3-2 defeat by Spain at Wembley in September, when La Roja demonstrated their attacking quality to secure all three points.
hat victory continued Spain’s recent dominance over England, having also beaten the Three Lions 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.
The two successive defeats will add extra motivation for Tuchel’s side, who must find a way to contain Spain’s attacking threats while improving their defensive organisation.
Spain, meanwhile, will approach the contest with confidence, having maintained an impressive run of competitive victories. The return of winger Lamine Yamal is another boost for the hosts as they seek to extend their winning run and consolidate their position at the top of the group.
Yamal’s pace, creativity and ability to trouble defenders in one-on-one situations could prove important against an England side expected to approach the match with greater attacking urgency.
For Tuchel, the challenge will be balancing England’s need to win with the discipline required to prevent Spain from exploiting spaces behind their defence.
Goalkeeper James Trafford is expected to start for England, adding another talking point ahead of the encounter as the visitors prepare for a difficult examination against one of Europe’s most dangerous attacking sides.
England will need greater efficiency in front of goal and improved defensive concentration if they are to reverse their recent fortunes against Spain.
The September meeting at Wembley showed that England possess the attacking quality to trouble the Spanish defence, but conceding three goals also exposed weaknesses that Tuchel will be keen to address.

Spain’s advantage lies not only in their home support but also in their confidence, consistency and recent success against England.
However, with qualification already secured, England have little to lose by taking the initiative, although an aggressive approach could leave them vulnerable to Spain’s counter-attacking threat.
Sunday’s encounter therefore presents more than a contest for three points. It is another opportunity for England to measure their progress under Tuchel against the reigning European champions, while Spain will be determined to reinforce their superiority in the group.
A draw would be enough for Spain, but England must win if they are to finish the group campaign above La Roja and send a statement ahead of the quarter-finals.
